shared_context.topic: Differential diagnosis of right lower quadrant abdominal pain

snippets.output: Right lower quadrant abdominal pain in a 33-year-old female can be caused by various conditions.
Appendicitis is a classic cause of right lower quadrant pain; it is an inflammatory condition of the appendix often preceded by symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, and loss of appetite.
snippets.notes: Pattern A: enumeration of features of one subject (appendicitis).
snippets.pattern_notes: Pattern A per notes: enumeration of features of appendicitis.

snippets.output: Diagnosis of appendicitis is typically made based on a combination of clinical presentation and imaging studies such as ultrasound or CT scans.
snippets.notes: Pattern A: diagnostic workup detail merged.
snippets.pattern_notes: Pattern A per notes: diagnostic workup details merged.

snippets.output: Ovarian torsion is a potential cause of right lower quadrant pain in women of childbearing age; it is a surgical emergency requiring prompt intervention to prevent ovarian necrosis.
snippets.notes: Pattern A: features of ovarian torsion merged.
snippets.pattern_notes: Pattern A per notes: features of ovarian torsion.

snippets.output: Endometriosis can cause right lower quadrant pain, particularly in women of childbearing age; it is a condition in which tissue similar to the lining of the uterus grows outside the uterus, leading to inflammation and pain.
snippets.notes: Pattern A: definition + features of endometriosis.
snippets.pattern_notes: Pattern A per notes: definition + features of endometriosis.

snippets.output: Adnexal torsion is a rare cause of right lower quadrant pain that involves the twisting of a fallopian tube or ovary, leading to ischemia and pain, and requires surgical intervention.
snippets.notes: Pattern A: features of adnexal torsion merged.
snippets.pattern_notes: Pattern A per notes: features of adnexal torsion.

snippets.output: Right-sided diverticulitis is a potential cause of right lower quadrant pain.
snippets.notes: Kept atomic (Pattern F) to separate the false epidemiology claim in atom 19.
snippets.pattern_notes: Pattern F per notes: isolated atom kept apart from false epidemiology claim.

snippets.output: Right-sided diverticulitis is more common in older adults.
snippets.notes: Right-sided diverticulitis is actually more common in younger adults, especially in Asian populations; left-sided diverticulitis is the form more common in older Western adults.
snippets.pattern_notes: Isolated false atom kept apart to avoid contaminating true claims.

snippets.output: Right-sided diverticulitis is more common in younger adults in Asian populations.
snippets.pattern_notes: Single atom, distinct checkable epidemiology fact about same topic.

snippets.output: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) is a rare tumor of the GI tract that can cause right lower quadrant pain, often associated with weight loss and abdominal distension.
snippets.notes: Pattern A: features of GIST merged.
snippets.pattern_notes: Pattern A per notes: features of GIST merged.

snippets.output: An intra-abdominal mass can cause right lower quadrant pain due to compression or irritation of surrounding structures.
snippets.pattern_notes: Pattern B per notes: causal chain (mass causes pain due to compression).

snippets.output: Intussusception can occur in adults and cause right lower quadrant pain, often with a palpable abdominal mass.
snippets.notes: Pattern A: features of adult intussusception merged. Kept separate from atom 29 to surface the children-only contextual divergence.
snippets.pattern_notes: Pattern A per notes: features of adult intussusception merged.

snippets.output: Intussusception is typically seen in children.
snippets.notes: Marquee ctx=false, gen=true: epidemiologically true that intussusception is mostly a pediatric condition, but contextually irrelevant/misleading as a differential for a 33yo female with RLQ pain.
snippets.pattern_notes: Single atom kept separate due to topic shift (pediatric context vs adult presentation).

snippets.output: Meckel's diverticulum is a rare congenital anomaly of the small intestine that can cause right lower quadrant pain, often associated with bleeding or obstruction.
snippets.notes: Pattern A: features of Meckel's diverticulum merged.
snippets.pattern_notes: Pattern A per notes: features of Meckel's diverticulum merged.

snippets.output: Idiopathic omental infarction is a rare cause of right lower quadrant pain in which the omentum becomes necrotic, often mimicking acute appendicitis.
snippets.notes: Pattern A: features of idiopathic omental infarction merged.
snippets.pattern_notes: Pattern A per notes: features of idiopathic omental infarction merged.

snippets.output: These conditions have varying presentations and prompt evaluation by a healthcare professional is required for accurate diagnosis and treatment.
